question.prompt: Two places are 600 km apart. The travel time t (h) and average speed v (km/h) of a high-speed train satisfy \(t=600/v\). If the travel time must not exceed 2.5 h, what is the minimum average speed in km/h?

solutions.explanation: \(600/v\le2.5\), with \(v>0\), so \(v\ge600\div2.5=240\). The minimum average speed is 240 km/h. When the distance is fixed, t is inversely proportional to v: the greater v is, the smaller t is.
solutions.title: Solve the travel-time inequality
Multiply the time inequality by v
Use the maximum allowed travel time
